text:
amy: Heads-up — CI started failing SAST on #4321. It flags a 'hardcoded key identifier' usage around our keystore wrapper. Not sure if it's a legit finding or scanner noise.

sec-bot: SAST report uploaded: vuln-id SAST-2026-0987. Path: services/secrets/keystore.go:42. Confidence: medium. Link: https://scans.redwood/sast/4321

bryan: can you paste the snippet? I looked at the PR briefly and I thought we pass only key names, not raw material.

amy: snippet: `client.Encrypt(ctx, "projects/proj/locations/global/keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/rdw-key", plaintext)` — scanner highlights the key resource string.

jordan: that's the full resource name, but it's not a secret. The scanner probably flags any KMS resource ARN-like string. Classic FP.

sam: plus we deploy that string from env/KMS_LOOKUP, it's not checked in. CI might be scanning generated compile-time constants from test fixtures though.

irina: two operational items: 1) we need an audit trail for decrypt requests for the service account CI uses, and 2) evidence/justification to suppress this finding for the compliance pack. Retention policy asks for 90d of KMS-access logs.

amy: ops question — do we already have KMS audit logs being exported to the logging bucket with 90d retention? I recall default retention is 30d.

bryan: infra: we have logs in cloud-logging but retention is 30d in the project. We can set an export sink to a long-term bucket (90/365) but that needs a perms change for the logging service account + bucket IAM.

jordan: that means an RBAC tweak: give logging.svcAcct writer on bucket and grant the CI service account only cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the specific key. Avoid broad roles.

sam: proposed commands (GCP) to add role to logging sink SA: ```
# grant writer to logging sink SA on bucket
gsutil iam ch serviceAccount:logging-sink@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com:objectCreator gs://redwood-compliance-logs
# set retention on bucket
gsutil retention set 90d gs://redwood-compliance-logs
```

irina: also add a policy to KMS key binding the CI service account: ```
# minimal KMS binding
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding rdw-key \
  --location=global --keyring=ring \
  --member=serviceAccount:ci-bot@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```

amy: good — we should also create a short-lived service account key pattern: CI uses workload identity (no long-lived SA keys). If any team still uses JSON keys we need rotation plan.

bryan: infra ticket created: INFRA-1298 to add sink + retention + SA perms. Assign to @bryan. ETA 2 days.

amy: for the SAST finding suppression: recommended evidence bundle items: 1) snippet showing it's a resource name, not a secret, 2) link to repo where value comes from env, 3) CI job log showing value masked, 4) audit log entry showing no decrypt calls during test.

jordan: I can produce (1) and (2) in a comment on the PR. irina, can you handle (3)/(4) once infra sets the sink?

irina: yes, I'll pull logs after sink exists and attach a filtered export for the compliance folder. Also will request a 90d retention exception until bucket is created.

sam: small dev note: we should add an eval to the SAST suppression whitelist with the rationale. Example suppression message: "FP - resource name, not secret. Value injected from env; CI uses WI. See INFRA-1298 and PR#4321." Include link to evidence.

amy: one more ask: incident response POV — if someone inadvertently checked in a real key material, how would detection look? We should create an alert on KMS Decrypt logs that triggers sec-oncall if decrypts happen from unexpected contexts (new IP or unknown SA).

bryan: agree. We can add a Cloud Logging alert: filter on protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND resource.labels.project_id="proj" AND NOT (principalEmail:"ci-bot@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com" OR principalEmail:"logging-sink@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com"). Alert to #sec-oncall and PagerDuty.

jordan: can we auto-block or rotate keys on suspicious decrypt? Rotation should be manual but playbook should include immediate key disable and rotate path. Add runbook link in INFRA-1298.

irina: created runbook stub: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/kms-decrypt-alert. Added steps: acknowledge alert, check audit log, disable key version, notify impacted teams, rotate key.

amy: OK next steps summary: 
- INFRA-1298: add logging sink + 90d retention + minimal SA perms (assigned to bryan).
- I will add SAST suppression comment + evidence placeholders to PR 4321 (amy).
- irina will attach audit evidence once sink exists (irina).
- jordan will draft KMS-decrypt alert + runbook additions (jordan).

sec-bot: label applied: security-triage, severity: low (suppression candidate).

bryan: I'll start infra changes today; ping here when PR comment live and when bucket created so I can validate writer perms.

amy: thanks all. I'll update PR and mark the SAST finding as 'suppression pending evidence'. :thumbsup:
